correctness.rationale: Hensel factorization and branch-by-branch valuation formula are exact; irreducibility makes any rational affine relation between distinct conjugate roots incompatible with finite Galois orbit under a positive p-power slope. Therefore all digit tails differ from each other and the original roots. Separate p-adic limits at these points establish independence of a, the constant, and de tail generators. The finite sample checker corroborates depths up to 4 for d=2 and up to 2 for d=3; the proof, not this sampling, certifies all depths.

value.rationale: Finite-depth p-kernel span rank is a canonical quantitative invariant of digit-recursive complexity; an infinite-rank theorem cannot specify how it grows. The theorem provides an exact dimension and basis at every depth for an entire degree-d family, including initial exceptional levels and root-affine collision rigidity, rather than an isolated computation.
